description: Optimize SGLang serving throughput for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark (284B total / 13B active MoE: 256 routed top-6 + 1 shared, hybrid Compressed Sparse Attention + Heavily Compressed Attention, MLA base, NVFP4/MXFP4 expert MLPs + fp8 everything else) on 4×H100 / SGLang 0.5.12.post1 (torch 2.10.0+cu128, sglang-kernel 0.4.2.post2 sm90/sm100) while preserving correctness. 4×H100 / TP=4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark for studying MLA / hybrid CSA/HCA attention / MoE / fp4-expert / RadixAttention / scheduler-level levers in SGLang's srt runtime. On H100 (sm_90) the fp4 experts run through SGLang's non-Blackwell fallback (dequant / mixed-precision GEMM) since NVFP4 tensor cores are Blackwell-only — an emulation-bound regime.

Optimize SGLang serving throughput for DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B total / 13B active MoE: 256 routed top-6 + 1 shared, hybrid Compressed Sparse Attention + Heavily Compressed Attention, MLA base, NVFP4/MXFP4 expert MLPs + fp8 everything else) on 4×H100 / SGLang 0.5.12.post1 (torch 2.10.0+cu128, sglang-kernel 0.4.2.post2 sm90/sm100) while preserving correctness. 4×H100 / TP=4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash for studying MLA / hybrid CSA/HCA attention / MoE / fp4-expert / RadixAttention / scheduler-level levers in SGLang's srt runtime. On H100 (sm_90) the fp4 experts run through SGLang's non-Blackwell fallback (dequant / mixed-precision GEMM) since NVFP4 tensor cores are Blackwell-only — an emulation-bound regime.

Optimize SGLang prefill/decode DISAGGREGATED serving for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 8xB200, scored on the geometric mean of continuation-turn tail latency AND tail inter-token latency (pooled P99 ITL) in a multi-turn agent workload. Two pools behind a conversation-sticky router: 4 GPUs of prefill instances and 4 of decode, joined by SGLang's NIXL transfer engine. 64 attention heads and a single MLA kv head, so TP=4 per pool is legal and TP=6 is not, which is why a 2P:6D topology cannot boot for this model. Why these axes and not throughput: vLLM's own docs say disaggregation does not improve throughput and make no TTFT claim -- what it controls is tail ITL rather than TTFT, and on a max_concurrency=1 workload a correct PD optimization scores NEGATIVE. Measured on 8xH100, PD improves continuation-turn p95 by 22.6% where the aggregated deployment has decode interference to remove, and loses on every single-turn shape.

Optimize vLLM throughput for DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8×B200 / vLLM 0.20.1+cu129. 1.6T total / 49B active MoE: 384 routed (top-6) + 1 shared, scoring=sqrtsoftplus, topk_method=noaux_tc, routed_scaling_factor=2.5, hidden_size=7168, 61 layers. Hybrid attention combines Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA, 4× compress) with Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA, 128× compress) — V4's headline innovation, claimed 27% / 10% FLOPs / KV-cache vs DSv3.2 at 1M ctx. MLA base: 128 heads, q_lora_rank=1536, head_dim=512, qk_rope_head_dim=64. Native fp4 (NVFP4/MXFP4) expert MLPs + fp8 everything else — Blackwell tensor cores natively accelerate both. Same architecture family as DeepSeek-V4-Flash, with 1.5× the experts and 2× the attn heads); ~865 GB on disk.

Optimize vLLM throughput for zai-org/GLM-5.2 on 8×B200 / vLLM 0.24.0. MoE with DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA): served by GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM (subclass of DeepseekV2ForCausalLM, model_type=glm_moe_dsa) on the DeepSeek-V3.2 DSA backbone (vllm/models/deepseek_v32/). ~256 routed experts (top-8), hidden 6144; MLA (q_lora_rank≈2048, kv_lora_rank≈512) + lightning-indexer sparse attention with index_topk_freq=4 and INTERLEAVED indexer RoPE (GLM-5.2-specific; DeepSeek-V3.2 uses NeoX); FP32 router MANDATORY; FP8 (e4m3 block-scaled) weights + FP8 KV cache (served with --kv-cache-dtype fp8). DSA GPU kernels are NVIDIA SM100 (Blackwell) only — hence B200, not H100. Architecture registered natively in vLLM 0.24.0 (registry.py GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM → deepseek_v2).

Optimize vLLM throughput for zai-org/GLM-5.2 on 8×B200 / vLLM 0.24.0. MoE with DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA): served by GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM (subclass of DeepseekV2ForCausalLM, model_type=glm_moe_dsa) on the DeepSeek-V3.2 DSA backbone (vllm/models/deepseek_v32/). ~256 routed experts (top-8), hidden 6144; MLA (q_lora_rank≈2048, kv_lora_rank≈512) + lightning-indexer sparse attention with index_topk_freq=4 and INTERLEAVED indexer RoPE (GLM-5.2-specific; DeepSeek-V3.2 uses NeoX); FP32 router MANDATORY; FP8 (e4m3 block-scaled) weights + FP8 KV cache (served with --kv-cache-dtype fp8). DSA GPU kernels are NVIDIA SM100 (Blackwell) only — hence B200, not H100. Architecture registered natively in vLLM 0.24.0 (registry.py GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM → deepseek_v2).

Optimize vLLM throughput for OpenAI gpt-oss-120b on 2×H100 / vLLM 0.19.1. Sparse MoE with 117B total / 5.1B active parameters, MXFP4-quantized expert weights (vLLM native _load_weights_mxfp4 path), GQA attention. Reference open-source MoE coverage in the throughput-opt suite.

Optimize vLLM throughput for moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 on 8×B200 / vLLM 0.20.1+cu129. Multimodal sparse MoE (KimiK25ForConditionalGeneration outer wrapper, text backbone DeepseekV3ForCausalLM-derived 'kimi_k2'): 61 decoder layers (first 1 dense, 60 MoE), 384 routed experts (top-k routing), 1 shared expert; bf16 weights (no FP8 quant); MLA attention with kv_lora_rank=512, hidden_size=7168, intermediate_size=18432; idle vision tower for text-only inference. ~595 GB on disk (64 safetensors shards).

Optimize SGLang serving throughput for Moonshot Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA linear attention + sigmoid-routed MoE) on 2×B200 / SGLang 0.5.10 (torch 2.9.1+cu12, sglang-kernel 0.4.1 sm90/sm100) while preserving correctness. 2×B200 (sm100) TP=2 Kimi-Linear-48B for studying KDA linear-attn / MoE / RadixAttention / scheduler-level levers in SGLang's srt runtime.

Optimize SGLang serving throughput for LLaDA2.0-mini-preview (block-diffusion MoE, 256 routed experts top-8) on 1×H100 / SGLang v0.5.18 while preserving the decode schedule. The first non-autoregressive execution mode in the optimize family: generation proceeds by unmasking positions inside a 32-token block under LowConfidence remasking, so forward passes per block are content-dependent and the levers are the diffusion loop's kernels, not an AR decode path.

Optimize SGLang serving throughput for MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7 (229B total / ~10B active sparse MoE: 256 experts top-8 routing, native FP8 weights, dense GQA full-attention) on 4×H100 / TP=4 / SGLang 0.5.10 (torch 2.9.1+cu12, sglang-kernel 0.4.1 sm90/sm100) while preserving correctness. 4×H100 MiniMax-M2.7 for studying MoE / FP8 expert / RadixAttention / scheduler-level levers in SGLang's srt runtime.

Optimize vLLM throughput for MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 on 4×B200 / vLLM 0.24.0. Sparse MoE: ~426B total / ~24B active parameters, 128 experts (top-4 routing) + 1 shared expert with sigmoid+routing-bias scoring, routed_scaling_factor=2.0; 60 decoder layers (3 dense + 57 MoE); HYBRID attention — dense full softmax attn layers 0-2, block-sparse GQA layers 3-59 via lightning indexer (sparse_block_size=128, sparse_topk_blocks=16, sparse_index_dim=128); GQA 64 q / 4 kv heads, head_dim=128, partial-rope (rotary_dim=64, theta=5e6); 1M context (max_position_embeddings=1048576); MXFP8-quantized weights (E4M3 + E8M0 128×128 block scales), bf16 activations, fp32 router; config declares num_mtp_modules=1 but the checkpoint ships NO MTP tensors (0 of 45,838 in its safetensors index, and 0 in the unquantized repo), so speculation here runs an EXTERNALLY trained EAGLE3 draft head instead -- Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3, a 1-layer dense Llama (~3.3B) sharing this target's embedding and LM head. THIS TASK RUNS IT: the verifier fixes --speculative-config on BOTH arms (eagle3, K=3), so enabling speculation is the verifier's action and never the agent's lever -- the agent can only make already-on speculation faster. Output is exact regardless (speculation's rejection-sampling guarantee), so a broken drafter shows up as lost throughput and as a fallen acceptance length, not as wrong tokens. Architecture registered natively in vLLM 0.24.0 (vllm/models/minimax_m3/, MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM).

Optimize vLLM throughput for MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 on 4×B200 / vLLM 0.24.0. Sparse MoE: ~426B total / ~24B active parameters, 128 experts (top-4 routing) + 1 shared expert with sigmoid+routing-bias scoring, routed_scaling_factor=2.0; 60 decoder layers (3 dense + 57 MoE); HYBRID attention — dense full softmax attn layers 0-2, block-sparse GQA layers 3-59 via lightning indexer (sparse_block_size=128, sparse_topk_blocks=16, sparse_index_dim=128); GQA 64 q / 4 kv heads, head_dim=128, partial-rope (rotary_dim=64, theta=5e6); 1M context (max_position_embeddings=1048576); MXFP8-quantized weights (E4M3 + E8M0 128×128 block scales), bf16 activations, fp32 router; native MTP module (num_mtp_modules=1) but baseline runs dense decode (spec decode is ZERO headline credit). Architecture registered natively in vLLM 0.24.0 (vllm/models/minimax_m3/, MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM).

Optimize SGLang prefill/decode DISAGGREGATED serving for MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 on 8xB200, scored on the geometric mean of continuation-turn tail latency AND tail inter-token latency (pooled P99 ITL) in a multi-turn agent workload. Two pools behind a conversation-sticky router, joined by SGLang's NIXL transfer engine. The engine is pinned to v0.5.18 by the MODEL: SGLang registers minimax_m3.py from v0.5.16 onward and 404s at every earlier tag, while disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py is present far below it -- so PD reached the released line long before this model did. 426B total / ~24B active MoE, MXFP8, served as 4P:4D with TP=4 per pool.

Optimize SGLang serving throughput for Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (sparse MoE: 397B total / 17B active, 512 experts top-10 routing, 3:1 hybrid linear+full attention, FP8 block-scaled experts weight_block_size=[128,128], GQA-2 head_dim=256) on 8×H100 / SGLang 0.5.10 (torch 2.9.1+cu12, sglang-kernel 0.4.1 sm90/sm100) while preserving correctness. 8×H100 / TP=8 Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 for studying MoE / FP8 expert / linear-attention / RadixAttention / scheduler-level levers in SGLang's srt runtime. Sister task to optimize_qwen3_5_397b_a17b_fp8_8xh100_open (vLLM) — same model + workloads for a cross-engine A/B.

Optimize vLLM throughput for Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 on 8×H100 / vLLM 0.19.1. Sparse MoE: 397B total / 17B active parameters, 512 experts (top-10 routing), 3:1 hybrid linear+full attention (45 linear + 15 full layers, like Kimi-Linear), FP8-quantized weights (block-scaled, weight_block_size=[128,128]), GQA-2 attention with head_dim=256. Multimodal architecture (vision tower idle for text-only inference). Highest-active-params MoE in the throughput-opt suite.

Optimize vLLM throughput for Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B on 1×H100 / vLLM 0.20.1 (+cu129 wheel, libcudart.so.12 / torch 2.11.0+cu128). Dense member of the qwen3_5 architecture family (architectures=Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, model_type=qwen3_5): 64-layer 3:1 linear+full hybrid attention (48 linear + 16 full), GQA-4 with head_dim=256, partial RoPE, multimodal (vision tower idle for text-only inference), native MTP head. Single-H100 dense hybrid-attention target for studying linear-attention / hybrid-KV / scheduler levers in vLLM 0.20.1.

Optimize vLLM prefill/decode DISAGGREGATED serving for Qwen3.6-27B on 2xH100 / vLLM 0.24.0+cu129, scored on the geometric mean of continuation-turn tail latency AND tail inter-token latency (pooled P99 ITL) in a multi-turn agent workload. Two pools behind a conversation-sticky router: ONE GPU of kv_producer and ONE of kv_consumer, joined by NixlConnector -- the SupportsHMA connector this hybrid-attention model requires, since vLLM disables the hybrid KV cache manager whenever --kv-transfer-config is set unless the connector subclasses it. The dense 27B member of the qwen3_5 family: 64 layers of 3:1 hybrid linear+full attention, 24 attention heads and 4 kv heads. Hardware sized to the model is the point: a TP=1 pool holds the whole model on one 80 GB device and the KV budget is a real constraint, which is the regime the split exists for.

Optimize SGLang prefill/decode DISAGGREGATED serving for Qwen3.6-27B on 2xB200, scored on the geometric mean of continuation-turn tail latency AND tail inter-token latency (pooled P99 ITL) in a multi-turn agent workload. Two pools behind a conversation-sticky router: ONE GPU of prefill and ONE of decode across the two GPUs, joined by SGLang's NIXL transfer engine. The model has 24 attention heads and 4 kv heads, so TP=1 per pool is the only split this model admits here; TP=6 is not legal for it at all. Why these axes and not throughput: vLLM's own docs say disaggregation does not improve throughput and make no TTFT claim -- what it controls is tail inter-token latency. A split only has something to relieve where the aggregated deployment has decode interference to remove, which is why the scored workload is a concurrent multi-turn one rather than any single-turn shape.

Optimize vLLM throughput for Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B on 1×B200 / vLLM 0.28.0+cu129. Dense 27B multimodal hybrid model (arch Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, model_type qwen3_5 — Qwen3.6 reuses the Qwen3.5 modeling code). 64 decoder layers in a 3:1 hybrid layout: 48 gated-delta-net linear-attention layers (GatedDeltaNetAttention, linear_conv_kernel_dim=4, 16 key / 48 value heads, head_dim=128, mamba_ssm_dtype=fp32 recurrent state) + 16 full-attention layers (GQA 24 q / 4 kv heads, head_dim=256, attn_output_gate, partial_rotary_factor=0.25, interleaved mrope). bf16 weights, hidden_size=5120, intermediate_size=17408, vocab 248320, 256K context (served at 16384). Idle vision tower (Qwen3_VisionTransformer, depth 27) loads at init for the text-only bench. Single-B200 compute-bound regime (no TP all-reduce).

Recover a decode-throughput regression on gpt-oss-120b (1xB200, TP=1) under async scheduling with an EAGLE3 speculative drafter. Throughput is simply lower -- no stall, no spike, no error, output bit-identical. The scored shapes are upstream's own reproduction (1024 requests at concurrency 512, 1024 in / 1024 out, no output-length jitter) and the same request shape at 384 and 256 concurrent requests, combined as a geometric mean; 128 concurrent requests is a guard, measured and never scored.

model.feature: MoE 120B (MXFP4) served at TP=1 on one B200, with a SEPARATE EAGLE3 draft head -- upstream's own reproduction configuration. TWO checkpoints, not one. The defect is host-side scheduling and is independent of model SHAPE, but not of the speculative METHOD: the engine refuses the combination this task needs unless the drafter is EAGLE/MTP.

description: Recover a decode-throughput regression on an MLA model served with an FP8 KV cache (DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4, 8xB200, data parallelism 8 with expert parallelism). The engine serves correctly and output is unchanged; only the decode path got slower. The loss is spread evenly across the sweep rather than concentrated in a stall or a tail, and it is invisible at small decode batch, which is why the scored workload issues every request at once.

model.feature: MLA attention with an FP8 KV cache at high decode batch; any 128-head MLA checkpoint of this shape reproduces, provided the deployment is data-parallel

description: Recover a decode-throughput regression that only appears when Qwen3-Next's own multi-token-prediction speculator is enabled (4xH100, TP=4). The engine serves correctly and the generated text is unchanged; the loss is a per-step host-side stall whose frequency tracks how often the running batch changes shape, which is why the scored workload runs 1000 requests at high concurrency rather than at a fixed batch size.

model.feature: Hybrid linear/full attention with a built-in MTP head; the speculator is what puts the defective path on the hot loop

description: Recover a large prefill-latency regression on Qwen3.5-4B under multimodal traffic whose request sizes vary: at the pinned parent, l2norm_fwd_kernel (python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/l2norm.py) declares the FLATTENED TOKEN COUNT `T` -- and `NB = cdiv(T, 2048)`, derived from it -- as `tl.constexpr`. Triton keys its kernel cache on every constexpr VALUE, so each distinct token count compiles a fresh cubin and the compile blocks the prefill that triggered it. The kernel is on the GDN linear-attention path: TritonGDNKernel.extend -> chunk_gated_delta_rule(use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True) -> l2norm_fwd on q and k. Upstream PR #31558 makes `T` a runtime scalar under @triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"]) and deletes `NB`, which the kernel body never reads.

model.feature: A hybrid linear-attention model that is ALSO multimodal, which is why a 4B fits a workload upstream ran on a 35B MoE across two H200s. Both halves are load-bearing and each is checked in-run rather than asserted. (1) LINEAR ATTENTION: its linear layers are Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet holding a RadixLinearAttention; the extend path is TritonGDNKernel.extend -> chunk_gated_delta_rule(..., use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True) -> l2norm_fwd on q and k. text_config.linear_key_head_dim = 128, which is <= 512 and therefore selects the l2norm_fwd_kernel branch -- the one with `T: tl.constexpr`; above 512 the code takes l2norm_fwd_kernel1, which has no T at all and no regression. 24 of its 32 layers are linear_attention. (2) VISION: config.json carries vision_config and image_token_id, so image resolution is what makes the prefill token count vary, which is upstream's own choice of variation source and the reason the symptom report can describe traffic rather than token counts.

description: Recover decode throughput on an MXFP4 mixture-of-experts model served by SGLang on Hopper. The Triton MoE kernel that runs the expert matmuls picks a launch configuration tuned for a different shape regime, and at the small per-expert row counts a decode step produces it splits work that does not need splitting. Output token throughput runs about a third below what the same kernel delivers once the configuration matches the shape; correctness is unaffected and aggregate GPU utilisation looks normal.

model.feature: MXFP4-quantised MoE: 24 layers, hidden 2880, intermediate 2880, 32 experts, top-k 4, alternating sliding(128)/full attention, quantization_config.quant_method = mxfp4. Read off the published config.json rather than assumed. 3 shards, 13,761,264,768 bytes (12.8 GiB); original/ and metal/ are not needed.

description: Recover a large streaming-decode throughput regression on gpt-oss-120b at concurrency 1. At the pinned commit the overlap scheduler's per-iteration work contains a device-to-host synchronization that cannot overlap the forward pass, and it costs roughly 1 ms per generated token. TWO independent repairs are known and both are legitimate: remove the synchronization (the min_new_tokens penalizer's boolean-mask indexing, measured at 1.39-1.41x) or restore the overlap the barrier introduced in PR #26380 removed (measured at 1.31-1.42x). The task scores recovered generated-token throughput and does not care which route a candidate takes.

model.feature: The model upstream's own top row uses. It is also a hybrid-SWA architecture, so it exercises the sliding-window half of the shared mapping the barrier protects.

description: Recover a speculative-decoding throughput regression on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with an external EAGLE3 drafter (1xH100, TP=1, async scheduling, 7 draft tokens, fp8 KV, 8 concurrent streams -- the regime upstream's own defect report measured in). The drafter's tokens are accepted far less often than this configuration used to manage, and throughput has fallen with it.

model.feature: 8B dense decoder driven with an EXTERNAL EAGLE3 drafter. The drafter is a second artifact rather than a head inside the target checkpoint, which is why this task declares one under [metadata.inference_bench.speculative_config].

Native DiffusionGemma-26B-A4B support on 2xH100: Hopper paged attention for batches mixing causal encoding and bidirectional denoising sequences through a public operator contract, and native block-diffusion serving at TP1 and TP2 with text, images, reads, chat, tools and preemption, with model quality, agreement with model-author recordings and engine regressions preserved.

Day-0 model support: land reliable, numerically faithful and efficient native GLM-5.3-Flash serving in SGLang on four B200 GPUs at the HighThroughput and LowLatency deployments, preserving relevant existing engine behavior

Native MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 support on 4xB200 in vLLM: MiniMax Sparse Attention (index-branch block selection and block-sparse attention, prefill and decode, BF16 and FP8 KV) implemented through a public operator contract and served natively in both deployments, with reasoning and tool-call parsing, model quality, efficiency and engine regressions preserved.

Native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 support on 4xB200: correct and efficient QSA, bounded-memory PLE, ordinary fresh-request/prefix reuse, and stateful MTP3 serving, with model quality and engine regressions preserved.

Add Stable Diffusion 3 (MMDiT text-to-image) support to SGLang's multimodal_gen diffusion engine. SD3 is a multimodal diffusion transformer (MMDiT) image generator with three text encoders (CLIP-L, CLIP-G, T5) and a 16-channel VAE. The pinned SGLang has no SD3 in multimodal_gen's registry; the task is to add native generation across the required precision and single-/two-GPU serving profiles, preserving request behavior and matching independent Diffusers references with fixed generation settings.

model.feature: MMDiT text-to-image diffusion. 3 text encoders (CLIP-L + CLIP-G + T5), 16-ch VAE, joint-attention DiT blocks. Output is an image (num_frames=1). Determinism via fixed seed + num_inference_steps + guidance_scale.
